CII Eastern Region
The Confederation of Indian Industry Eastern Region (CII ER) comprises of the states of Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Orissa and West Bengal. The Eastern Region witnessed substantial economic growth in recent times and is now booming with confidence. The eastern region of India is a land of huge potential and is endowed with plenty of rich minerals, forests, productive and fertile soil and rich cultural heritage. Given the available natural resources and quality manpower, the key growth engines in this part of the world are Iron & Steel, Power, Mines & Minerals, Tourism, Agro & food processing, Infrastructure, IT & ITES, Petrochemicals, Leather, Real Estate, Retail and Cement. The Eastern states have potential for large-scale production and export of spices, jute, and other agro products. A spurt in investments coming to these states is an indication of a bright future for trade and industry in the region. There has been a continuous improvement in the hard and soft infrastructure. The growth of IT & ITES, Healthcare and Tourism in the eastern states coupled with rapidly developing educational sector unfolds unique advantage adding to the rich intellectual base of the region. The CII National Theme for 2023-24 was decided as Towards a Competitive and Sustainable India@100: Growth, Inclusiveness, Globalisation, Building Trust. Dovetailing with the national theme, the states and the region have decided to work on the theme of EAST - Economic Action for a Sustainable Tomorrow. The states have taken up three priority areas for the year focusing on Competitiveness, Sustainability, Growth, Livelihood and Inclusion, Globalisation and Building Trust and have committed to work in these spaces. They are working extensively with the CII Centres of Excellences and would make strong cases of advocacy to their governments in various verticals apart from the various initiatives they would undertake in the year.

Key Initiative of Jharkhand State Office
CII Jharkhand Council has been making concerted efforts in the direction of bringing growth and development in the State right from its inception in the year 2000. The Council facilitated Department of Industries, Govt. of Jharkhand in coming up with an Industrial Policy of Jharkhand in the year 2001. The Council also partnered Govt. in successfully organizing Udyog Mela 2007 in Ranchi & facilitating Jharkhand pavilion in IITF 2008(India international Trade Fair) at New Delhi. In order to enhance the competitiveness of industry members, CII Jharkhand Council continues to organise number of training programmes, major Conferences, seminars, workshops on Manufacturing, Agro & Food Processing, Environment, Mining & Coal, Social Development & Community Affairs, Behavioral Skills & Information Technology, as well as interactions with key Govt. Officials at Ranchi ,Jamshedpur and also at Bokaro. The Council recently called on the Hon’ble Chief Minister & Deputy Chief Minister of Jharkhand and presented them with CII Vision document : Jharkhand @ 2022, a Sustainable Vision document encompassing hope & aspiration of the people of Jharkhand. The insight of the document is aimed at enabling the key decision makers to plan and implement findings at the grass root level, leading to sustained growth and development of the State.
Key Initiative of West Bengal State Office
CII - West Bengal State Council has been regularly working towards creating a right platform for interaction, meetings while taking up contentious issues with the relevant authorities. The Council’s resolute to strengthen the very fundamentals of economy and build a resonating state remains unabated. West Bengal State Council is also focusing on a) District Development b) Abating Climate Change and c) Disaster Management - the three key areas which require a lot of attention. In addition to the above, the Council has been regularly organizing programs covering different issues & subjects for the benefit of our members. West Bengal @ 2022 is one of the other major initiatives wherein the Council has tried to identify the potential areas of growth and benchmark them for continuous development.

CII Excellence Awards for Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Eastern Region
CII (ER) has an annual award scheme to recognize the excellence of its members in the spheres of safety sector during the year. The excellence in Safety Health & environment (SHE) Award is to acknowledge the vision and exemplary commitment the CEO and his team has for Environmental Responsibility, concern for occupational Health and Safety of employees and society as a whole. The objective of this Award is to evaluate an Organization’s interest towards the well being of its employees through adequate measures, not only for the Regulatory requirements, but also as a part of the Management’s Commitment towards ensuring that the workforce is adequately protected through effective Safety, Health & Environment measures. Physical safety assessments are done by the certified safety auditors as a part of the selection process. The Award ceremony is organised in August every year coinciding with the annual CII Eastern Region Safety Symposium & Exposition. Based on the assessments and scores, Star Rating certificates in the scale of 5 are also given to all applicants.

Andaman and Nicobar
The Andaman and Nicobar Islands, an archipelago in the Bay of Bengal, is a union territory. Consisting of 527 small and large islands, the Andamans are dotted with a a 100-km coastline and covered with dense forests. Sitting close to an international trade corridor, the Andamans, where the rate of literary is high and society heterogeneous, is a bright candidate for a thriving container port. The Government of Andaman and Nicobar has created an enabling environment and announced several policy measures and incentives to attract investment across sectors.
The GSDP at current prices for 2014-15 stood at Rs 5721 crores with a growth rate of 10.89 per cent over previous year.
The Andamans’ growth potential is stated to be high in areas such as tourism, energy, shipping, minerals & mining, livestock and marine products. A greater thrust on MSMEs, and also services industries, particularly tourism, are some of the recommended initiatives which will take the union territory to the high-growth orbit. A roadmap to maximize its unconventional energy resources is another recommended step.
It is widely felt that the archipelago will win a place of prominence in domestic as well as global value chain by leveraging its proximity to countries such as Thailand, Myanmar and Indonesia, and Indian port cities like Kolkata, Chennai and Vizag, and also by integrating with the East Coast Industrial Corridor (including Chennai-Vizag Industrial Corridor), Amritsar-Kolkata Industrial Corridor and North East Myanmar Industrial Corridor.

Arunachal Pradesh
Arunachal Pradesh is a thinly populated hilly tract lying on the north-east part of India comprising roughly 83,573 square kilometers.
The GSDP at current prices for 2015-16 stood at Rs 19473 crores with a growth rate of 18.81 per cent over previous year.
The state is rich in flora, fauna, power and mineral potential. It is bounded by independent countries on the three sides and by Assam and Nagaland in the south. The long international border comprises of Bhutan on its west, the Tibet region of China on its northern and north east border and Myanmar on the eastern border. The economy in this hill state is facing with severe problems due to lack of industriliasition and limited scope in other areas for any gainful activities. The sectors of focus include industries based on agricultural, horticultural and plantation produces, non-timber forest produces, bamboo, cane (rattan), medicinal plants / herbs, aromatic grass, tea, coffee etc. Emphasis is also being given to textiles (handlooms and power looms), handicrafts and sericulture; mineral-based industries such as ferro-alloys and cement plants; electronics, pharmaceuticals, power, food processing, engineering and allied industries, tourism and hospitality, art and craft, etc. The State Government has partially implemented computerization of commercial tax department.

Resurgent Arunachal: Integrated Approach to Security and Development
CII and SIDM participated in the "Resurgent Arunachal: Integrated Approach to Security and Development" seminar, organized at the Likabali Military Station on 21–22 March 2025.
A joint presentation by CII-SIDM, delivered during the seminar, delved into the vital theme of economic growth and self-reliance for Arunachal Pradesh. It emphasized the importance of policies and initiatives that can drive industrial development in key sectors. The presentation also explored how enhancing connectivity, promoting local entrepreneurship, developing skills, and fostering collaboration among stakeholders can unlock the immense potential of the state’s diverse resources.
A key area that emerged during the seminar was the empowerment of youth. CII and SIDM stressed the necessity of investing in the younger generation, advocating for initiatives that support skill development, entrepreneurship, and job creation. This focus on youth is particularly critical in a state where the demographic dividend can be harnessed for meaningful and sustainable economic growth.
The dialogue also underscored the importance of collaboration among various stakeholders, including government bodies, private sector entities, and civil society organizations. A shared commitment to implementing an integrated strategy will be essential in addressing the unique cultural, ethnic, and ecological contexts of the state, while also ensuring that security considerations are adequately managed.
The seminar served as a platform for fostering new partnerships aimed at creating a roadmap for Arunachal Pradesh as a self-reliant and vibrant state. With concerted efforts, the economic prosperity of Arunachal Pradesh can be driven by youth empowerment, market linkages, technological interventions, and sustainable resource management.

Assam
Assam is the gateway to the North East India. Its topography, rich biodiversity, forest cover and fertile land etc., make Assam a bright candidate for a global agro-processing and tourist destination. The GSDP at current prices for 2014-15 stood at Rs 198098 crores with a growth rate of 11.45 per cent over previous year.
Agriculture makes a significant contribution to its domestic sectors accounting for more than a third of Assam’s income. Of a population of 267 million in Assam, 69% constitute the working force. Tea and oil & gas are two predominant industries of Assam which accounts for about 15% of the country’s crude oil output and 50% of India’s total on-shore production of natural gases which may be used for production of fertilizers, electricity, petrochemicals and fuel in the industrial sector. Energy, bamboo, handloom and handicraft are the other promising sectors. Assam has 7 Integrated Infrastructure Development Centres (IIDC), 2 Industrial Growth Centres (IGC), 1 Export Promotional Industrial Park (EPIP), 5 Industrial Parks and 9 Industrial Areas. Assam Industrial Development Corporation Limited (AIDC) has been incorporated in 1965 and its main objective is to promote industries or entrepreneurs. The Government is facilitating the industrialization in the state with enabling policies.

The Conclave was addressed by Secretary NEC, RD RBI, CGM SBI, CGM NABARD. Commissioner Industries Govt of Assam, Chairman Pollution Control Board, ED NEDFi among other esteemed dignitaries. The discussions focused on strengthening MSMEs through easier access to finance, digital transformation, regulatory simplification, formalisation, market linkages and sustainable growth.
The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) organized a series of Business-to-Business (B2B) and Business-to-Government (B2G) meetings during the visit of a high-level delegation comprising leading logistics companies from Thailand and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to Guwahati from 15–18 June 2026. The visit was aimed at exploring new business opportunities, fostering strategic partnerships, and strengthening trade and logistics linkages between Northeast India and key international markets in Southeast Asia and the Middle East.
The delegation called on the Hon'ble Chief Minister of Assam and held comprehensive discussions on the State's vision for transforming Assam into a major logistics, trade, and investment hub for Northeast India. The meeting highlighted the Government's continued focus on strengthening infrastructure, improving ease of doing business, and leveraging Assam's strategic location as the gateway to Southeast Asia under India's Act East Policy. The delegation also held detailed interactions with the Chief Secretary and the Additional Chief Secretary, Government of Assam, where discussions centred on the State's infrastructure development, multimodal logistics ecosystem, industrial growth, and emerging investment opportunities.
CII also coordinated sector-specific meetings with senior officials of the North Eastern Regional Agricultural Marketing Corporation (NERAMAC), Container Corporation of India (CONCOR), Tea Board of India, Spices Board of India, and other key institutions. In addition, the delegation engaged with representatives from more than fifty industries across sectors including tea, agri and food processing, logistics, manufacturing, exports, infrastructure, and trade.

Bihar
Bihar is surrounded by Nepal in the north, West Bengal in the east, Uttar Pradesh in the west, and Jharkhand in the south. The state enjoys a unique location-specific advantage because of its proximity to the vast markets of eastern and northern India, access to ports such as Kolkata and Haldia, and to raw material sources and mineral reserves from the neighbouring states. In 2022-23, Bihar’s GSDP at current prices is projected to be Rs. 7.45 trillion (US$ 97.39 billion). The state’s GSDP expanded at a CAGR (in Rs.) of 10.43% between 2015-16 and 2022-23. Bihar has witnessed strong growth in per capita net state domestic product. At current prices, per capita NSDP of the state grew at a CAGR of 10.73% (in Rs.) between 2015-16 and 2020-21.
Bihar is one of the strongest agricultural states in the country. The percentage of population employed in agricultural production in Bihar is around 80%, which is much higher than the national average. It is the fourth largest producer of vegetables and the eight largest producers of fruits in India. Food processing, dairy, sugar, manufacturing, and healthcare are some of the fast-growing industries in the state. The state has planned initiatives for the development of other sectors such as education and tourism, and also provides incentives for information technology and renewable energy projects.
The state has a large base of cost-effective industrial labour, making it an ideal destination for a wide range of industries. According to the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), cumulative FDI inflows in Bihar were valued at US$ 168.08 million between October 2019-June 2022. Total merchandise exports from the state stood at US$ 2,308.60 million in 2021-22, and US$ 1,258.97 in 2022-23 (till August 2022).

pages.text:
Chhattisgarh
Chhattisgarh shares its borders with Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra to the west, Uttar Pradesh to the north, Odisha and Jharkhand to the east, and Telangana (newly formed from Andhra Pradesh) to the south.
As per the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), the Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) of Chhattisgarh at current prices stood at Rs. 5.07 trillion (approx. US$ 61.4 billion) for the year 2023–24 (AE - Advance Estimates). Between 2015–16 and 2023–24, the GSDP at current prices has grown at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of about 9.5%.
Chhattisgarh continues to be one of the few power-surplus states in India. The Korba district, often referred to as the "Power Capital of India", houses several thermal power plants. As of January 2024, the state’s total installed power generation capacity stood at 13,989 MW, comprising:
Private sector: ~9,034 MW
State utilities: ~2,012 MW
Central utilities: ~2,943 MW
Chhattisgarh is rich in mineral resources and ranks among the top producers of coal, iron ore, dolomite, and limestone. The state continues to be the only producer of tin concentrates in India, contributing over 35% of the country’s tin ore reserves. It also has significant deposits of bauxite and quartzite.
In terms of exports, merchandise exports from Chhattisgarh were valued at:
US$ 1.28 billion in FY20
US$ 2.32 billion in FY21
US$ 3.39 billion in FY22
US$ 2.45 billion in FY23
(Source: DGCIS & Ministry of Commerce and Industry)
The state continues to promote industrial growth through progressive policies. While the Industrial Policy 2014–19 laid the foundation, new initiatives under the Industrial Policy 2019–24 offer incentives across sectors including IT/ITeS, food processing, renewable energy, logistics, mining, and biotechnology.
Chhattisgarh ranks among the top 10 Indian states in the ease of doing business index, as per the DPIIT-State Reform Action Plan rankings, owing to its single-window clearance system, simplified regulations, and proactive governance.

Jharkhand
Jharkhand is one of the leading states in terms of economic growth. At current prices, Jharkhand’s gross state domestic product (GSDP) stood at Rs. 3.63 trillion (US$ 48.63 billion) in 2021-22. Jharkhand is one of the richest mineral zones in the world and boasts of 40% and 29% of India's mineral and coal reserves, respectively. Due to its large mineral reserves, mining and mineral extraction are the major industries in the state. Jharkhand is rich in mineral resources such as coal (27.3% of India’s reserves), iron ore (26% of India’s reserves), copper ore (18.5% of India’s reserves), uranium, mica, bauxite, granite, limestone, silver, graphite, magnetite and dolomite. Jharkhand is the only state in India to produce coking coal, uranium, and pyrite. With 25.7% of the total iron ore (hematite) reserves, Jharkhand ranks second among the states. It is closer to the ports of Kolkata, Haldia and Paradip which helps in transportation of minerals.

pages.text:
Meghalaya
Located in the North Eastern part of India, Meghalaya is chiefly an agricultural state with 80% of its 3 million people depending on the farm sector for sustenance. Rich in flora, fauna, power, and mineral deposits, Meghalaya is a state where major crops are rice and maize. It is also known for its horticultural crops such as orange, lemon, pineapple, guava, litchi, banana, jack fruits and temperate fruits such as plum, pear, peach, etc. potato, ginger etc. Meghalaya is also home to rivers and streams – something which is an additional source of hydro-electricity generation – and vast deposits of coal, limestone, granite, clay and other minerals.
The GSDP at current prices for 2015-16 stood at Rs 27305 crores with a growth rate of 13.46 per cent over previous year.
In 2004-05, the contribution of the services sector in the state’s GSDP at constant prices was $382.7 million, which reached $ 682.3 million in 2014-15.The State Government has identified a few sectors of focus – industries based on agricultural, horticultural and plantation produce; bamboo, medicinal plants / herbs, tea, etc; mineral-based industries (eg. ferro-alloys, cement Plant, steel processing etc.); IT-based enterprises, pharmaceuticals; food processing; tourism (tourism infrastructure including resorts, hotels, restaurants etc.) and hospitality; hydropower; art and craft industries. The Travel and Tourism Department in Meghalaya is responsible for 0.1% of India’s GDP. Tourism development is undertaken as to ensure sustainability and conservation of the states environment and natural resources. The Government is working on creating basic infrastructure for tourism development and also act as a facilitator for private investment in this sector. As part of its focused exercise to increase ease of doing business, the Meghalaya Government has initiated a number of processes such as registration for VAT, payment of taxes, way-bills administration; transit passes, processing of VAT returns, etc.

The Mizoram Government is setting up a Special Economic Zone (SEZ) to encourage economic growth with assistance from the North Eastern Council. The State Government has also adopted a Rs 270-crore New Economic Development Policy to boost the state’s economy and livelihood of the people. The policy aims to lead Mizoram from a subsistence-based economy to a market-based economy.

pages.text:
Sikkim
Sikkim, India’s second-smallest in geographical size, is a fast developing State. Its Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) between 2004-05 and 2014-15 expanded at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 18.34 percent to US$ 2.1 billion whereas the Net State Domestic Product (NSDP) expanded at a CAGR of 17.74 per cent to US$ 1.74 billion
Driven primarily by tertiary sectors, the State's economy is largely agrarian which is based on terrace-farming of rice and cultivation of crops such as maize, millet, cardamom, buckwheat, pulses, spices, cereals, oranges, tea etc.
Although Sikkim has only 11% of land under productive cultivation, it has achieved the distinction of becoming India’s first State to be certified as “fully organic” by the Union Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and some accredited agencies.
On 18 January 2016, the Prime Minister, Mr Narendra Modi, who launched the Sikkim Organic, logo, handed two commendations to the state in recognition of its extraordinary journey towards total organic farming. As of now, 76,392 hectares of Sikkim’s cultivated land is certified as fully organic.
Sikkim’s thrust areas are eco-tourism, MSME, handicrafts & handloom, medicinal & forest based, horticulture & floriculture, food processing, pharmaceuticals, honey & biotechnology.
The Sikkim Government’s mission is to make tourism the principal means of livelihood for its 6 lakh-plus people and develop high-skilled human resources needed for the sector.
Clearly, the state Government aims to give higher impetus to rural tourism as well to make sure rural communities get significant economic benefits. Home stay is one of the integral components of rural tourism. As many as 660 home stays are currently being run.
The mission is designed to provide tourists with a “Feel Sikkim from Within” experience – Sikkim’s way of life, environment, happiness index and cultural strengths.
The Sikkim Government also encourages wellness tourism and pilgrimage tourism for which it regularly conducts a variety of activities at different levels.
Sikkim, which has a hydro potential to produce 8,000 MW, has given green light t29 hydroelectric power plants to independent power producers which are at various stages of construction.
As part of its Mission to provide uninterrupted power supply to all connected consumers as well as unconnected households by way of Intensive Electrification and System Strengthening, Sikkim has launched a comprehensive scheme to strengthen the distribution and transmission system. It aim is also to provide electricity with free connections to all rural and BPL households.

Tripura
Thanks to its strategic geography, Tripura is seen as the Gateway to South East Asian economies. Bounded by Bangladesh on its south, west and north, Assam and Mizoram, Tripura is endowed with natural resources such as rubber and natural gas, and also possesses vast potential for forest-based industries. Tripura’s forest resources include bamboo, medicinal herbs and wood, which are being utilised for setting up of forest-based industries. Surplus power is a big plus for businesses, especially food processing. With Bangladesh being there on three sides of Tripura, export promotion and cross-border trade is an important area. Export promotion, particularly in Bangladesh, is another area of focus. Natural gas, rubber and tea, tourism, etc, are potential sectors for development in the state. Since Tripura is rich in natural gas reserves and surplus in power, the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas has come out with the North East Hydrocarbon Vision 2030 to fuel development of the entire region’s hydrocarbon potential. The state is keen to to build stronger infrastructure, bio-tech parks, food parks, rubber park, IT parks. The recent launch of trans-shipment operations in Chittagong in Bangaldesh aims to boost trade and facilitate seamless movement of goods. India was for long seeking transit and transshipment facility to carry goods to Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura, from West Bengal through a shortened route via Bangladesh.

These entrepreneurs have become an integral part of the robust value chain in the sector. Tripura has about 15 million trees, mostly on private lands and 70% of these trees are in the North Tripura District. The State Government of Tripura has already notified the Tripura Agarwood Policy 2021 to fulfil the State’s vision for creating Tripura, a hub for Agarwood products in the country and is moving towards creating a sustainable, quality focused and market-driven Agarwood economy. With this objective, the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) in association with NTFP Centre of Excellence, Department of Forest, Government of Tripura organized the 4th International Agarwood Conclave and Buyer and Seller Meet 2024” with the theme “Enhance your business with the essence of Tripura Agarwood” on 2nd-4th December 2024 at Agartala, Tripura. The Conclave was inaugurated by Prof (Dr) Manik Saha, Chief Minister of Tripura. In his inaugural address, the Hon'ble Chief Minister mentioned that Agar is the symbol of Tripura's economic growth, and the Agar cultivation has links to the state's tradition and culture. Agar is generating livelihood support to thousands of families and active participation of women in this sector is paving way for their financial independence, he added. Shri Animesh Debbarma, Forest Minister of Tripura in his address as the Guest of Honour spoke about the potential of the agarwood sector in Tripura and requested to scale up the annual buyer-seller meet to reach out to a larger audience globally. Shri J. K. Sinha, IAS Chief Secretary of Tripura mentioned about reducing the compliance burden and easing norms for agar export. Mr R K Samal, IFS, Principal Chief Conservator of Forests & Head of Forests Force & Principal Secretary, Department of Forests mentioned about the bottlenecks in the current export license and the CITES Permit Process and have suggested modification for ease of doing business. He added that the presence of multiple stakeholders, lack of timelines and absence of real time information act as hinderance for export of agarwood. Mr Prasada Rao Vaddarapu, IFS, Director, NTFP Centre of Excellence, Department of Forests, Government of Tripura gave a detailed presentation on the Agarwood sector in Tripura outlining the strategy for its growth. Mr. Sanjay Garhwal, Member, CII North East Council & Chief Operating Officer, OTPC proposed the Vote of Thanks. The 4th International Agarwood Conclave and Buyer-Seller Meet 2024 had participation from 70 buyers and 38 sellers from across the country.

West Bengal
West Bengal shares its borders with Jharkhand, Bihar, Odisha, Sikkim, and Assam. The state also shares international borders with Bangladesh, Bhutan, and Nepal. The Bay of Bengal is in the south of West Bengal. At current prices, gross state domestic product (GSDP) of West Bengal is estimated at Rs. 17.13 trillion (US$ 221.39 billion) in FY 2022-23.
In FY23 (until August 2022), the total exports from the state stood at US$ 5,830.91million. West Bengal exported key items such as iron & steel and marine products. West Bengal is the second largest tea-producing state in India and is home to the globally acclaimed Darjeeling tea variety. West Bengal is the largest producer of rice in India.
Its location advantage makes the state a traditional market for eastern India, the Northeast, Nepal, and Bhutan. It is also a strategic entry point for markets in Southeast Asia. The cost of operating a business is lower in Kolkata than in other metropolitan cities.
West Bengal has abundant natural resources of minerals and suitable agro-climatic conditions for agriculture, horticulture, and fisheries. It is in vicinity to mineral rich states like Jharkhand, Bihar, and Odisha. It offers excellent connectivity to the rest of India in terms of railways, roadways, ports, and airports.
As of August 2022, West Bengal had a total installed power generation capacity of 10,656.38 MW, of which 5,997.95 MW was under state utilities, 2,912.02 MW under private sector and 1,746.41 MW under central utilities.
Between October 2019-June 2022, FDI inflows in West Bengal stood at US$ 1,048.25 million.

Chandigarh
Chandigarh, India’s first planned city and known as the ‘City Beautiful’, is a Union Territory (UT) and joint capital of Punjab and Haryana. Its economy is overwhelmingly service-driven, with the tertiary sector contributing 88.8% to Gross Value Added (GVA) in 2023-24 — the highest among all Indian states and UTs. The Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) at current prices was ₹6,253,564 (Lakhs) in 2023-24 with the UT growing at a CAGR of 11.74 per cent at constant prices over the past 3 years. The per capita income (at current prices) stood at ₹5,05,134 in FY 2023-24, one of the highest in the country. Anchored by strong growth in IT/ITeS through the Rajiv Gandhi Chandigarh Technology Park (an SEZ), education, healthcare, retail, trade & repair services (35.4% of services GVA), real estate & professional services (25.7%), and financial services, Chandigarh is steadily evolving as a hub for innovation, knowledge-based industries, and sustainable urban development. The city is witnessing growing momentum in sectors such as IT, healthcare, education, and startups, supported by improved digital infrastructure and stronger industry–academia collaboration. Chandigarh continues to focus on green mobility, renewable energy adoption, and citizen-centric governance, further strengthening its position as one of India’s most pogressive and liveable cities.

pages.text:
Delhi
Delhi is the administrative capital of India, the seat of power, and a major hub of trade and commerce. It continues to be one of the fastest-growing urban economies in the country. As per the Economic Survey of Delhi 2025–26, the Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) of Delhi at current prices is estimated at
₹13.27 trillion in 2025–26, reflecting a robust growth of 9.42% over 2024–25. The per capita income of Delhi is estimated at
₹5,31,610 in 2025–26, registering a growth of 7.92% and remaining around 2.5 times higher than the national average, highlighting the city’s strong income levels and high standard of living. Delhi’s economy is predominantly service-driven, with the tertiary sector contributing 86.32% to Gross State Value Added (GSVA), while the secondary and primary sectors contribute 12.88% and 0.80% respectively, reinforcing Delhi’s position as a knowledge-based and service- led economy. The state has maintained a consistent revenue surplus, estimated at
₹9,661 crore in 2025–26, demonstrating fiscal prudence and strong economic fundamentals. The total budget outlay for 2025–26 stands at
₹1,00,000 crore, with significant allocations towards transport, social welfare, water supply, education, and healthcare to support inclusive development. The Government of NCT of Delhi continues to focus on building a progressive and business-friendly economic environment. Delhi has a well-developed infrastructure ecosystem, including airports, highways, and one of the largest metro rail systems in the world. Public transport continues to expand, with the electric bus fleet increasing from 2,150 in April 2025 to 4,338 in March 2026, and average metro ridership reaching about 67 lakh passengers per day, strengthening sustainable urban mobility. The industrial and power sectors have also shown steady growth. The manufacturing sector remains a key component of the secondary sector, with GSVA rising to
₹50,144 crore in 2025–26. Power demand has grown significantly, with peak demand reaching 8,442 MW, and side by side renewable energy capacity has increased to 509 MW, supporting the city’s sustainability goals. Delhi remains a major tourism hub, ranking 6th in foreign tourist visits in 2024 with a share of 9.55%, reflecting its continued importance as a cultural and economic destination. In social and urban infrastructure, Delhi has achieved notable progress. About 93.5% of households have access to piped water supply, and water infrastructure continues to expand to meet growing demand. Delhi’s healthcare system has also been strengthened, with extensive infrastructure to improve accessibility and quality of care. Delhi has one of the largest shares of skilled workforce in the country, making it highly suitable for knowledge-based economic activities such as IT/ITeS, design, research and development, and financial services. With strong connectivity, robust infrastructure, and a diverse economic base, Delhi offers significant opportunities for investment, particularly in the services and emerging technology sectors. CII Delhi has been actively engaging with the industry & government in Delhi, making key policy representations across sectors, including inputs on Delhi’s Startup and Industrial Policies. It has also published sectoral reports on Viksit Delhi 2047, Real Estate, Digital MSME Credit, Commercial Financing, and Education & Skills. It actively facilitates policy consultations, investment promotion engagements, competitiveness initiatives, capacity building programs, industry roadshows and sustainability initiatives across the state. CII Delhi continues to play a pivotal role in fostering a conducive business environment and strengthening the growth and competitiveness of industry in the region.

pages.title: Haryana
pages.text:
Haryana
Haryana today stands among India’s leading economic and industrial powerhouses and is steadily evolving into a future-ready, globally competitive, innovation-driven, and sustainable growth engine for the country. Backed by its strategic location in the National Capital Region (NCR), strong manufacturing base, rapidly expanding services economy, progressive governance framework, and world-class connectivity, the state has emerged as one of the most preferred destinations for domestic and global investments. Guided by the Government’s long-term development roadmap, Haryana Vision 2047, the State aims to transform itself into a trillion-dollar-plus economy with focus on industrial competitiveness, future-ready infrastructure, innovation, sustainability, skilling, urban transformation, and governance reforms. Despite accounting for only around 1.3% of India’s geographical area, Haryana contributes nearly 3.7% to India’s GDP and continues to rank among the leading States in per capita income, industrial productivity, exports, and investments. Haryana’s Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) has crossed
₹12 lakh crore, while the State’s per capita income, estimated at over
₹3.5 lakh annually, remains significantly above the national average. The secondary and tertiary sectors together contribute nearly 80% of the State’s Gross Value Added (GVA). Haryana has developed globally competitive ecosystems across sectors such as automobiles and auto components, IT & ITeS, electronics and ESDM, Global Capability Centres (GCCs), renewable energy, logistics, pharmaceuticals and medical devices, textiles, real estate, food processing, agritech, defence manufacturing, and emerging technologies including AI and digital innovation. The state also hosts strong traditional manufacturing clusters in plywood and paper products, ceramics, engineering goods, scientific instruments, handloom and textiles, along with a rapidly growing MSME ecosystem. The automobile and auto components industry continues to form the backbone of Haryana’s manufacturing economy, with the state contributing significantly to India’s production of passenger vehicles, tractors, two-wheelers, construction equipment, and mobile cranes. Industrial hubs such as Gurugram-Manesar, Faridabad, Panipat, Sonipat, Karnal, Hisar, and Yamunanagar support extensive supply chains and MSME ecosystems, while Gurugram has also emerged as a major hub for GCCs, startups, IT services, fintech, consulting, and innovation-led enterprises. Infrastructure development remains central to Haryana’s Vision 2047 strategy with over 26,000 km of road network, strong rail connectivity, access to the Dedicated Freight Corridor (DFC) and Delhi–Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC), and proximity to the Indira Gandhi International Airport. Haryana is also investing in multimodal logistics, industrial corridors, digital infrastructure, smart urbanisation, renewable energy, and future- ready industrial parks to support long-term growth. pages.title: Himachal Pradesh
pages.text:
Himachal Pradesh
Himachal Pradesh (HP) has transformed from a predominantly agrarian economy into one of India’s fastest-growing industrial hubs. The state is bordered by Jammu and Kashmir to the north, Punjab to the west and southwest, Haryana to the south, Uttar Pradesh to the southeast, and China to the east. Known as the “Fruit Bowl of India” and “Dev Bhoomi” (Land of the Gods), Himachal Pradesh is renowned for its breathtaking natural beauty and scenic landscapes. The state recorded 10.1 per cent nominal GSDP growth and 6.4 per cent real growth in FY2024-25. The State’s Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) at current prices for FY2024-25 (First Revised) is estimated at
₹2,30,587 crore, up from
₹2,09,385 crore in FY2023-24. At constant (2011– 12) prices, the GSDP stands at
₹1,44,656 crore for FY2024-25. Himachal Pradesh’s economy has undergone a significant structural transformation, with the secondary and tertiary sectors now contributing over 86 per cent of the Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP). The state has also emerged as a leader in horticulture, particularly in apple production, while diversifying into floriculture, mushroom cultivation, and sub-tropical fruits. Additionally, steady progress in renewable energy and hydropower has further strengthened revenue generation and enhanced energy security. Himachal Pradesh has one of the largest Drug Manufacturing Hubs in terms of volume of finished products and the 1 st Medical Devices Park in North India has been sanctioned in Nalagarh. The Baddi-Barotiwala- Nalagarh (BBN) industrial belt has emerged as a key manufacturing hub for various sectors, especially pharmaceuticals. Through the Himachal Pradesh Tourism Policy, 2019 the state is offering attractive incentives to promote tourism investment with a focus on theme-based tourism opportunities such as eco-tourism, adventure tourism and spiritual tourism. Exports in Himachal Pradesh grew from 1.3 Billion dollars in 2019-20 to 2.3 billion in 2023-24 indicating a CAGR of 13 per cent. According to NITI Ayog’s Export Preparedness Index 2022, HP ranked 15 th amongst all States and UT’s and 2 nd amongst Himalayan states receiving a score of 52.25. Himachal Pradesh has consistently strived towards a sustainable and inclusive development model, prioritizing green industries and providing robust support for MSMEs. The industrial Policy of 2013 clearly states this vision and the Sustainable Development Goals India Index 2023-24 ranks Himachal Pradesh at number five amongst all Indian states by aggregating its performance across goals. As per the Business Reforms Action Plan Survey 2022 conducted by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, in both categories of reforms – business centric and citizen centric, Himachal Pradesh comes under the category of Aspirers based on the State’s compliance to the action plan. The government has a single window clearance policy in place. It improved its ease of doing business ranking from 17 in 2015 to 7 in 2019 showing a clear direction towards improvement.

pages.title: Jammu & Kashmir
pages.text:
Jammu & Kashmir
Jammu & Kashmir, known as “Paradise on Earth” and famous for its mountainous landscape, derives significant economic support from its thriving tourism sector. The economy of J&K has shown steady growth in recent years, with real GSDP expected to grow by about 5.82 per cent in 2025–26 (AE at constant prices) and the size of the economy estimated at around
₹2.86 lakh crore (at current prices). The economy is largely service-driven, with the tertiary sector contributing 61 per cent to GVA, followed by the primary sector at 20.45 per cent and the secondary sector at around 18.52 per cent. The per capita income has increased significantly to approximately
₹1,68,243 in 2025–26, reflecting improved economic conditions. The Union Territory has been growing at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 4.47 per cent at constant prices over the period 2019-20 to 2024-25. The Industrial Policy 2021–30, along with the Start-up Policy 2024–27 and the single-window clearance mechanism, has played a crucial role in promoting industrial development and investment in the Union Territory. These initiatives have led to the establishment of several new industrial units, boosting employment and economic activity. Jammu & Kashmir is witnessing rapid infrastructure development, with numerous road, rail, and airport projects underway to improve connectivity. A number of major infrastructure projects and several highway development initiatives are being executed to strengthen the transport network. Improved connectivity through expressways, tunnels, and rail links is expected to further enhance trade and tourism in the region. The government is also promoting tourism infrastructure including ropeways and destination development projects. The region also continues to focus on hydropower development, supported by substantial natural potential. The installed power capacity of J&K has increased to around 3,600 MW, while the Union Territory has an estimated hydropower potential of about 18,000 MW and significant solar energy potential. With diverse agro-climatic conditions, the region offers vast opportunities in horticulture and food production, with strong growth in fruit production and related exports. This has created significant investment potential in food processing and allied sectors. The scenic beauty, favorable climate, and improved infrastructure make J&K an attractive destination for tourism, while sectors such as hydropower and renewable energy offer promising opportunities for future growth.

pages.title: Punjab
pages.text:
Punjab
Punjab, often referred to as the ‘Granary of India’ is one of India’s key agrarian and industrial state with strong infrastructure, skilled human capital and a highly entrepreneurial population. The state spans over an area of 50,362 sq. km and is home to over 3 crore people. Punjab has recorded a Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) of
₹83,863,661 lakhs for the year 2024-25 at current prices and has grown at a Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR at constant prices) of 6.3% between 2020–21 and 2024–25. Per capita income in FY25 stood at Rs 2,21,197 (at current prices). Its strong connectivity includes around 1,47,862 km of road network, 2,265 km of rail network, two international airports (Amritsar and Chandigarh) and 4 domestic airports (Bathinda, Jalandhar, Ludhiana and Pathankot). It is also supported by a robust logistics ecosystem comprising of 2 air cargo terminals, 5 inland container depots, and other allied infrastructure facilities. Historically anchored in agriculture, the state’s economy has evolved into a strong industrial base with 52 focal points, three operational Special Economic Zones (SEZs), and around 1,974.53 hectares of available industrial land. The state has actively pursued reforms to make it easier and more attractive to do business. These efforts include rationalised power tariffs, a robust single-window clearance mechanism, progressive labour reforms, and other investor-friendly initiatives. To support investment and industrial growth, the state has introduced the Industrial and Business Development Policy 2026, positioning itself as the first state in India to allow investors to ‘self-design’ incentive packages from 20 fiscal incentive options. The state has also introduced several sector-focused policies including the Startup Policy, Retail Investment Policy, Integrated Logistics Policy, Affordable Housing Policy, Electric Vehicle Policy, IT/ ITES Policy, Biotechnology Policy, Tourism Policy, and Renewable Energy Policy amongst others. The Punjab Bureau of Investment Promotion functions as a one-stop clearance system, facilitating investor approvals through coordination across departments such as pollution control, excise and taxation, labour, factory licensing, boiler registration, town and country planning, land, and power.

pages.title: Rajasthan
pages.text:
Rajasthan
Rajasthan, the largest state in India by area, is in the northwestern part of the subcontinent. It borders six major states in the northern, western, and central parts of India. Rajasthan is a natural corridor between the wealthy northern and the prosperous western states, making it an important trade and commerce centre. The natural resources, policy incentives, strategic location and infrastructure in the state are favourably suited for investments in sectors such as cement, tourism, agriculture and allied industries, mineral and mineral processing industries. The state has an agricultural economy with nine agro-climatic zones and various types of soil that help during the cultivation of crops. The GSDP at current prices is estimated to reach
₹18.75 lakh crore in the year 2025-26, up from
₹17.01 lakh crore in the year 2024- 25, showing a growth rate of 10.24 per cent. The GSDP at constant (2011-12) prices is estimated to reach
₹9.82 lakh crore in the year 2025-26, up from
₹9.04 lakh crore in the year 2024-25, showing a growth rate of 8.66 per cent. The Per Capita Income, a crucial indicator of standard of living, is estimated to increase by 9.32 per cent to
₹2,02,349 at current prices. Rajasthan ranks first in India in the production of oilseeds, rapeseed and mustard and is the second largest producer of garlic, nutri-coarse cereals, coriander, and cumin. The state is the leading producer of cement-grade limestone in India. Production of limestone stood at 79,236 thousand tonnes in 2023-24. The state's installed power capacity has increased from 27,283.83 MW (March, 2025) to 31,556.43 MW (December, 2025). Renewable energy showed strong performance, with solar capacity reaching 9,898 MW and wind capacity reaching 4,416.12 MW, together accounting for 45.36 per cent of total installed capacity up to December, 2025. According to the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows in the state stood at Rs. 28,688 crore (US$ 3,267 million) between April 2000-June 2025. Total merchandise exports from Rajasthan stood at Rs. 33,976 crore (US$ 3.86 billion) in FY26 (April-July 2025) and gems & jewellery and engineering goods accounted for a majority share in the overall exports from the state.

pages.title: Uttar Pradesh
pages.text:
Uttar Pradesh
Uttar Pradesh, located in northern India, is the country’s most populous state. Spread across nearly 240,000 sq. km, the state accounts for about 7.3% of India’s geographical area and contributes approximately 9% to the national gross domestic product as of 2024-25. With a Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) of approximately INR 2,97,822,351 (lakhs) in FY 2024-25, the Government of Uttar Pradesh has embarked on an ambitious mission to become a USD 1 trillion economy within the next five years. The state contributes significantly to India’s MSME ecosystem with more than 90 lakh MSME units and is emerging as a major hub for electronics manufacturing, defence production, food processing, textiles, renewable energy, EV manufacturing, and logistics. Traditionally an agrarian economy, Uttar Pradesh remains one of India’s leading producers of wheat, sugarcane, milk, potatoes, rice, and food grains. Agriculture and allied sectors continue to employ a large share of the workforce and contribute 26.82 per cent to the state’s gross state value added (GSVA). At the same time, the state has rapidly diversified into manufacturing and services (contributing 25.91 per cent and 47.25 per cent respectively) through strong policy reforms, infrastructure expansion, and industrial investments. A major strategic initiative driving industrial growth in the state is the Uttar Pradesh Defence Industrial Corridor, one of India’s flagship defence manufacturing corridors under the Government of India’s Atmanirbhar Bharat vision. The corridor spans key nodes including Lucknow, Kanpur, Jhansi, Aligarh, Agra, and Chitrakoot, attracting investments in aerospace, defence equipment, ammunition, drones, and advanced manufacturing. The corridor is expected to strengthen indigenous defence production, promote MSME participation, generate large-scale employment, and position Uttar Pradesh as a leading defence manufacturing hub in India. The state’s industrial growth has been supported by transformative infrastructure projects including the Purvanchal, Bundelkhand, Ganga and Yamuna Expressways dedicated freight corridors, expanding metro connectivity, and multiple international airports including Jewar International Airport, expected to become one of Asia’s largest airports. The services sector contributes nearly half of the state’s economy and continues to grow rapidly in IT & ITES, tourism, healthcare, education, banking, fintech, retail, logistics, and digital services.

pages.title: Uttarakhand
pages.text:
Uttarakhand
Uttarakhand was formed on 9 November 2000 as India’s 27th state, carved from northern Uttar Pradesh. Located in the Himalayan foothills, it shares international borders with China in the north and Nepal in the east, and state borders with Himachal Pradesh in the northwest and Uttar Pradesh in the south. The state has two administrative divisions — Kumaon and Garhwal — comprising 13 districts. Dehradun, the capital, lies in the Doon Valley on the Ganga-Yamuna watershed and is known for its scenic landscape. Rich in natural resources, Uttarakhand has abundant water, forests, glaciers, rivers, and snow-clad peaks. With literacy rates above the national average, the state offers quality human capital. The per capita income for Uttarakhand for 2024-25 stood at Rs. 2,74,064. The State’s Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) at current prices for FY2024-25 is estimated at
₹37,824,453 lakhs with the state recording a real growth of 6.61 per cent in FY2024- 25. Uttarakhand has been rapidly transforming itself into an economic powerhouse. With an unbeatable combination of single-point clearances, competitive land prices, cheap power, highly skilled manpower and stable law & order situation, the state has emerged as a preferred Investment destination. The government is actively upgrading infrastructure and government to business service delivery to stimulate agriculture, industry, and services in line with the state’s geographic strengths. Uttarakhand is recognized as a top performer in the “Achievers” category for Ease of Doing Business, driven by a fully operational Single Window Clearance System. The state has prioritized technology-driven reforms, offering online approvals and reducing physical touchpoints to enhance the investment climate. It has emerged as a key investment destination for manufacturing, tourism, and infrastructure. An abode to the Himalayas and the Ganges, the state is home to 5 top tourism destinations of India. The state has also emerged as one of the major investment destinations for manufacturing in the country with the secondary sector contributing to more than 45 per cent of the State's GSDP for the FY2024-25. The government's investor friendly policies are poised to attract further investments in the state. Strategically located near the National Capital Region (NCR), the state features seven expansive industrial estates spanning over 8,000 acres, high export growth, and 100% rural electrification supported by affordable, green hydropower. Enhanced by transparent land allotment policies, excellent multi-modal transit connectivity, and a thriving tourism sector that draws tens of millions of annual visitors, Uttarakhand offers a seamless onboarding ecosystem for investors looking to capture long-term strategic advantages. The state also offers massive commercial opportunities in minerals, floriculture, and horticulture.

pages.title: Andhra Pradesh
pages.text:
Andhra Pradesh
Andhra Pradesh is the eighth largest state in India covering an area of 1,60,205 square kilometers. The State has a coastline of 974 km, the second longest among all the states of India after Gujarat. The State is in the process of transformation and emerging as Sunrise state with growth strategies and targets are being set to achieve them in defined timeframe under Vision 2029. Government adopted mission based approach for targeting double digit growth on a sustainable basis. Sustaining double digit growth for the next 14 years is imperative to ensure that Andhra Pradesh will be one among the top three performing states by 2022, the best in the country by 2029 and the best global destination by 2050. Amaravati, the capital of Andhra Pradesh, is envisioned to be a city of world-class standards with a vision of increasing Andhra Pradesh's prominence in the world.
The prime focus of the state is to promote infrastructure in the State and develop cities like Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupathi with the best infrastructure facilities like metro rail, outer ring roads and international airports, IT hubs and simultaneously promote the identified smart cities. Andhra Pradesh is endowed with rich natural resources. It is endowed with large number of mineral resources and it is called as a mineral store house. The major minerals include bauxite, lime stone, barytes, sea sand, quartz, oil and natural gas, dolomite, steatite, calcite, low grade iron ore, etc. The State has 6 varieties of agro-climate conditions with 5 different types of soils. It is a pioneer in the production of spices, oil palm, tomato, chilies, turmeric, citrus, tobacco, egg production. The State leads in the cultivation of mango, banana, cashew, and flowers. The State contributes 50% of the country’s marine exports. The State is emerging as a preferred tourism destination and with top tourist spots located across the state. The State has an excellent Road Connectivity with 4-lane or 6-lane connecting all the urban cities of state. Andhra Pradesh has longest seacoast with one major port - Visakhapatnam, 12 intermediate and minor ports. Krishnapatnam is the largest private sector port in India. The State has well connected airport facilities at Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada, Tirupathi and Rajahmundry and Puttaparty. The textile and apparel industry is set to grow into a multibillion dollar opportunity. Andhra Pradesh is the third largest cotton producer in the country. Government is aiming at promotion and developing a strong and vibrant textile industry in handloom, power loom, and textile and apparel sectors. The Government of Andhra Pradesh is committed to catapulting the State into the top slot of industrial development in India, with a thrust on manufacturing which includes: renewable energy, special purpose machines, high precision machined components, parts used in defence and space research, bio-technology, IT hardware, and automation.

pages.title: Karnataka
pages.text:
Karnataka
The Future being made in Karnataka
Karnataka is situated on the south west region of India. Bordered by the Arabian Sea and the Lakshadweep Sea to the west, Goa to the north-west, Maharashtra to the North, Telangana to the North-East, Andhra Pradesh to the east, Tamil Nadu to the South East and Kerala to the South-west, the State covers an area of 191,976 square kilometres (74,122 sq mi) – about 5.80 percent of the total geographical area of India. It is the seventh largest State of India by area and the eighth largest state in India by population.
Karnataka state renowned as Knowledge, Innovation and R&D Capital of India. One of the largest global tech hubs, it's a hub for Hi-Tech sector's with a thriving economy.
The state GDP stands at US$ 120 billion and is growing at a healthy 7% pa. It has an industrial output of US$ 61.5 billion and a cumulative FDI of US$18.30 billion since April 2000- September 2015. The value of total exports of the state is US$ 52 billion which contributes to 13% of India's exports to the world. This position of strength is vastly driven by three strong growth factors. Firstly, the location advantage that easily connects Bangalore directly with the most of the world; Secondly, the solid foundations that aid knowledge capital here: the state has many building blocks to its credit - It is the largest bio technology hub In India, It has the largest number of R&D centers, The largest number of medical institutes, industrial training institutes; largest software technology parks and 3rd largest engineering colleges in India.

pages.text:
Kerala
Kerala is located along the coastline to the extreme southwest of the Indian peninsula, flanked by the Arabian Sea on the west and the mountains of the Western Ghats on the east. The State has a coastline of 580 km. Spread over 38,863 square km, it is bordered by Karnataka to the north and northeast, Tamil Nadu to the east and south, and the Lakshadweep Sea to the west. The State is divided into 14 districts with the capital being Thiruvananthapuram. Malayalam is the most widely spoken language and is also the official language of the State. Kerala has a high literacy and social indicators on par with developed economies.
Agriculture remains a key sector in the Kerala economy. It is a leading agricultural state in the country and the largest producer of rubber, pepper, coconut and coir. In 2014-15, the state contributed 69 per cent and 73 per cent to India's total rubber and pepper production, respectively.
In order to encourage more manufacturing units, Kerala has taken some major steps in upgrading the skills of labour and for boosting entrepreneurship. Skill training has begun making strides in the State. The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) sector is fast emerging into a major income generating and employment providing sector in Kerala with relatively lower investment. MSME sector can lead the State economy by increasing exports through quality production techniques and products.
Recognizing the importance of infrastructure, the State has during the last four years given a thrust to major projects like the Kochi Metro, Vizhinjam Port and Kannur Air Port. These projects are expected to bring about major transformation in the State economy.

pages.text:
Puducherry
Puducherry, formerly known as Pondicherry, is a Union Territory (UT) of India. Puducherry lies in the southern part of the Indian Peninsula. The areas of Puducherry and Karaikal are bound by the state of Tamil Nadu, while Yanam and Mayyazhi (Mahe) are enclosed by the states of Andhra Pradesh and Kerala respectively. All four districts of Puducherry are located in the coastal region. Five rivers in Puducherry district, seven in Karaikal, two in Mahé and one in Yanam drain into the sea, but none originates within the territory.
Puducherry is the 29th most populous and the third most densely populated UT in India. As it is a Union Territory, the governance and administration of Puducherry falls directly under the Central government. However, along with Delhi, Puducherry is one of two union territories in India that is entitled by special constitutional amendments to have an elected legislative assembly and a cabinet of ministers, thereby conveying partial statehood.
Puducherry is one of the most popular Indian tourist spots for national and international tourists. Puducherry has a literacy rate of 86.55%. Pondicherry University is a central university located in Puducherry. Other colleges include Jawaharlal Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education & Research (JIPMER), Indira Gandhi Medical College and Research Institute (Government of Puducherry), Mahatma Gandhi Medical College and Research Institute, National Institute of Technology, Puducherry, Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Institute of Engineering and Technology, and Pondicherry Engineering College.
Puducherry has seven well established industrial estates with comprehensive infrastructure facilities housing many of the global brands in the manufacturing and services sectors.
,
Puducherry is well connected to most of the major cities/towns of India by road. Puducherry and Chennai are well linked through picturesque East Coast Road (ECR). Puducherry’s Karaikal Port has 5 berths in 597 acres. The port’s capacity is 25 MT with mechanization. It handles all types of cargo. Operation of smaller aircraft from Puducherry Air Port expected to resume shortly. The nearest international airport is at Chennai, 162 km from Puducherry.

Tamil Nadu
Tamil Nadu lies in the southernmost part of the Indian Peninsula and is bordered by the union territory of Puducherry and the South Indian states of Kerala, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh. It is bounded by the Eastern Ghats on the north, by the Nilgiri, the Anamalai Hills, and Kerala on the west, by the Bay of Bengal in the east, by the Gulf of Mannar and the Palk Strait on the southeast, and by the Indian Ocean on the south. It also shares a maritime border with Sri Lanka.
Tamil Nadu is the 2nd largest economy and one of the fastest growing States in India. On the global scale, Tamil Nadu is ranked as 35th largest economy on PPP basis (larger than the economies of countries like Romania, Ukraine, Vietnam, Bangladesh, New Zealand, Norway, Finland, Denmark, Sri Lanka, Bulgaria, Uzbekistan, and Afghanistan.) The State is one of the major growth engines of the country with an average growth rate of over 9% in the last 9 years. It is also one of the top three FDI destinations in India. It stands first in terms of number of factories, numbering about 40,400.
Tamil Nadu currently has 20 industrial parks which are established and maintained by SIPCOT in places like Hosur, Cheyyar, Ranipet, Bargur, Siruseri, Cuddalore, Thoothukudi, Irungattukottai, Sriperumbudur, Manamadurai, Oragadam, Pudukottai, Pillaipakkam, Nilakottai, Vallam-Vadagal, Gangaikondan, Gummidipoondi, Perundurai, Thervoykandigai, and Mappedu. It also has 12 new industrial parks in various stages of development. The State has 78 Special Economic Zones and 30,000 acres of land bank available for industrial development.
Chennai is the capital of Tamil Nadu. The capital city is home to some of Fortune 500 companies including: Ford, Delphi, Visteon, Hyundai, Daimler Nokia, DELL, Flextronics, Nissan, Toshiba, Yamaha, Mitsubishi and Komatsu. The city has India’s largest electronics cluster (located in Sriperumpudur).
Tamil Nadu is the most urbanised state in India with a power generating capacity of about 18200 MW, the second largest among Indian states. It boasts of the largest telecom bandwidth and tele-density in India with 14.8 tbps (3 submarine cables), and over 8.4% of total subscriber base. The State has the third largest highways and rail network, 4 modern sea ports, and 23 minor ports.
Tamil Nadu’s Vision 2023 document targets to place the state in the league of Upper Middle Income countries in terms of economy and social development.

pages.title: CII Goa
pages.text:
Goa
Goa, nestled on the Konkan Coast roughly 600 kilometers south of Mumbai, boasts a vibrant tapestry of natural beauty, robust infrastructure, and burgeoning industries. Spanning 3,702 square kilometers, the state offers excellent social, physical, and industrial infrastructure, seamlessly integrated with high-speed virtual connectivity.
Goa's international airport efficiently caters to its global recognition as a premier leisure destination. Furthermore, a second greenfield international airport is under development in Mopa, with an ambitious goal of handling 30 million passengers annually by its final phase (Phase IV). The state also boasts a well-developed port infrastructure, facilitating seamless movement of goods and services.
While tourism remains a cornerstone of Goa's economy, attracting both domestic and international visitors, the state is actively fostering a diversified economic landscape. Goa has established a strong foundation in the pharmaceutical industry and is emerging as a key player in knowledge-based sectors like biotechnology and information technology.
The state government, aligned with the "Make in India" initiative, actively promotes the establishment of non-polluting and employment-generating industries. Their focus areas for greenfield investments encompass a wide range, including knowledge-based industries and R&D centres, pharmaceuticals & biotechnology, integrated educational hubs, light engineering, aviation, aerospace, and defence, information technology (research, hardware, and electronics), agro & food processing industries and shipbuilding.
Goa boasts a population density exceeding the national average, with 425 people per square kilometer as per the latest census. Additionally, the state demonstrates a high literacy rate of 88.70%, with a narrowing gender literacy gap over the past five decades.
Goa's economic growth is fueled by the exceptional performance of key sectors like fishing, agriculture, tourism, and pharmaceuticals. As of 2021-22, Goa's Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) stood at a robust Rs 826 billion at current prices. The state also enjoys one of the highest per capita Net State Domestic Products in India.
The state's commitment to infrastructure development extends beyond passenger travel. Goa's international airport boasts two terminals: a 700,000 sq ft single passenger terminal and a dedicated cargo terminal currently under development in phases. This upcoming cargo terminal has the potential to establish Goa as a regional logistics hub, specializing in the crucial cold chain segment for international cargo movement.
Goa has a well-established shipbuilding industry, playing a significant role in India's maritime sector. The state houses several shipyards, including the Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL), a leading government-owned shipyard known for constructing defence vessels and commercial ships. With its strategic location on the western coast and skilled workforce, Goa is poised to further develop its shipbuilding capabilities and attract investments in this sector.
Goa's strategic location, well-developed infrastructure, and commitment to sustainable growth position it as a thriving hub for leisure, industry, and knowledge-based activities. As the state continues to diversify its economy, attract investments, develop its cargo handling capabilities, and expand its shipbuilding industry, Goa's future promises to be as bright and dynamic as its vibrant cultural tapestry.

Gujarat
Gujarat, located on the western coast of India, has the longest coastline of 1,600 kms in the country. With 42 ports, 18 domestic airports, one international airport, 106 product clusters and 60 notified special economic zones (SEZs), Gujarat is one of the fastest growing economies in the country.

Gujarat received the highest Foreign Direct Investments of US$ 21.89 billion among all states in FY21 constituting 30% of the total equity inflows.

The industrial sector in the state comprises over 800 large industries and 453,339 micro, small and medium enterprises making it a hub for investments and trade.
Adding to this, a large scale investment is expected in Gujarat in the near future as part of the US$ 90 billion Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC).

pages.text:
Madhya Pradesh
The Confederation of Indian Industry Western Region (CII WR) comprises the states of Goa, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra. These states with their distinctive niche, potential and capabilities, have contributed significantly to the growth story of India. Abundant natural resources, industrial strengths, sound infrastructure, investor-friendly ambience and availability of skilled manpower make this region attractive to investors.
The major manufacturing industries located in the region include basic iron and steel, auto & auto components, engineering, chemical & petrochemicals, gems & jewellery, textiles, agro & food processing, cement and pharmaceuticals, to name a few. The region has a thriving service sector comprising banking & financial services, legal services, transportation, tourism, entertainment and healthcare. It is home to important financial institutions such as the RBI, SEBI, BSE, NSE and the corporate headquarters of numerous Indian companies and multinational corporations.
Gujarat was among the top achievers in the DIPP’s Business Reforms Action Plan (BRAP) 2020 rankings, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra were recognized as the achievers and Goa was categorized as an aspirer state. Gujarat and Maharashtra have been the frontrunners in terms of industrial development. Madhya Pradesh on the other hand has a vibrant agriculture-based economy and has recently ventured on the path to industrialisation. Goa’s economy is driven by the sectors like mining, tourism and pharmaceuticals.
CII Western Region serves a membership base of over 2,300 direct members and a much wider base of indirect members through its 34 regional and local member associations. In 2024-25, CII Western Region adopted the theme - ‘Globally Competitive India: Partnerships for Sustainable and Inclusive Growth’. CII in the region hosts some of the major national and international summits, conferences, exhibitions, business missions, trade delegations, training workshops and SME development meetings to serve its membership.

Maharashtra
Having a 720-km-long coastline along the Arabian Sea, Maharashtra occupies the western and central part of India and is fortified naturally by Sahyadri and Satpuda mountain ranges. The state is surrounded by Gujarat to the north west, Madhya Pradesh to the north, Chhattisgarh to the east, Telangana to the south east, Karnataka to the south and Goa to the south west. For administrative convenience, the state has been divided into 36 districts and six revenue divisions.
With a population of 11.24 crore, as per Population Census 2011 and having a geographical area of about 3.08 lakh sq. km, the state ranks second in terms of population and third in terms of geographical area. Maharashtra is one of the highly urbanised states in India.
Mumbai, the state capital is not only home to leading corporate houses and firms but also to Asia’s oldest Stock Exchange, the Bombay Stock Exchange.
To develop the industrial sector, the government placed thrust on sectors like Agro & food processing units, Textile machinery manufacturing, Information Technology (IT) & IT Enabled Services (ITeS), Electric vehicles, Industry 4.0 (Artificial Intelligence (AI), 3D printing, Internet of Things (IoT) & Robotics, Nanotechnology), Integrated Data Centre Parks, Electronic Systems Design & Manufacturing (ESDM) and Semi-conductor fabrication.
The state has been adopting varied measures for enhancing ‘Ease of Doing Business’. MIDC is offering ready-to-move-in factory environment under Plug & Play Infrastructure complete with advanced utilities and affordable pricing structure with sectoral tailoring. The grand response garnered in ‘Magnetic Maharashtra 2.0 Investors Summit’ demonstrated that the state remains the favoured destination for investments owing to well-developed infrastructure, technological advancement, availability of skilled manpower, connectivity to major areas and ample natural resources.

Dadra & Nagar Haveli
The union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli was merged with the neighbouring union territory of Daman and Diu to form the new union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu on January 26, 2020. It is one of the eight Union Territories (UT) of India. The region is spread over an area of 603 sq km. As per the 2011 census, the population is 5.86 lakhs. Natural endowments such as favourable weather conditions and scenic expanses, have made the territory an attractive tourist destination.
The UT shares borders with the Arabian Sea, Maharashtra, and Gujarat. The UT has a strong presence in the textile, plastic, and marine product sectors. Total merchandise exports from the UT stood at US$ 4.55 billion in FY23. The UT is an established base for the textile and plastic industries. It leads the country in integrated textile plants and polyester hubs and accounts for 80% of India’s texturizing yarn production. It is a leader in plasticisers and contributes to 28% of India’s plastic production in the form of aerospace, households, medical, greenhouses, defence, and non-conventional energy. The UT has a well-developed social, physical, and industrial infrastructure. It has a domestic airport that connects it to the cities of Mumbai and Ahmedabad and has a minor port infrastructure. Between October 2019-December 2023, FDI inflows in Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu stood at US$ 175.63 million.

Telangana
Telangana is the 29th State of India, formed on the 2nd of June 2014. The State has an area of about 1,15,000 sq km and has a population of over 3.5 crore. Telangana is surrounded by Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh in the North, Karnataka in the West and Andhra Pradesh in the South and East directions. The capital of Telangana is Hyderabad and major cities of the State include: Warangal, Nizamabad, and Karimnagar. The State has 31 districts: Adilabad, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Hyderabad, Jagtial, Jangaon, Jayashankar Bhupalapally, Jogulamba Gadwal, Kamareddy, Karimnagar, Khammam, Kumarambheem Asifabad, Mahabubabad, Mahabubnagar, Mancherial, Medak, Medchal–Malkajgiri, Nagarkurnool, Nalgonda, Nirmal, Nizamabad, Peddapalli, Rajanna Sircilla, Ranga Reddy, Sangareddy, Siddipet, Suryapet, Vikarabad, Wanaparthy, Warangal Rural, Warangal Urban and Yadadri Bhuvanagiri.
Two important rivers of India, the Godavari and Krishna, flow through the state, providing irrigation.
Telangana's state domestic product is estimated to be Rs. 8.43 lakh crores (US $ 130 billion) for the year 2018-19. Accounting for about 65% of the GSDP, services industry is the major sector of Telangana, followed by industry (16%), and agriculture (18%). Its per capita income is Rs.1,58,360/- for 2016-17. Telangana is home to several major manufacturing industries such as bulk drugs, pharmaceuticals, agro-processing, cement & mineral-based industries, high precision engineering, textiles, automobiles and auto components industry, spices, horticulture, poultry farming, biotechnology, defence equipment, etc.
The State has over 1 lakh small, medium and large scale industries providing employment to 17.5 lakh people in the organised sector. Telangana’s industrial policy intends to provide a friendly business regulatory environment. In order to have an effective industrial clearance mechanism, the State government has strengthened Telangana State Industrial Project Approval and Self-certification System (TS-iPASS) by way of legislation. A Right to Single Window Clearance, on the lines of the Right to Information, has been introduced for the speedy approval of industrial projects. The government supports skill development programmes targeted at industrial sector jobs under the ambit of the Telangana State’s Skill Development Mission (TASK) and the Telangana State Accelerated SSI Skills Training (T-ASSIST) program. Telangana offers various incentives under Telangana State Industrial Development and Entrepreneur Advancement incentive scheme. The incentives include: stamp duty reimbursement; land cost rebate; land conversion cost, power cost reimbursement, investment subsidy, VAT reimbursement, interest subsidy, seed capital for first generation entrepreneurs, training and skill development, and quality/patent support.
In addition to the policy measures, incentives and initiatives provided by the state, Telangana has advantages that make the state as potential manufacturing hub in India.
Telangana is the 29th State of India, formed on the 2nd of June 2014. The State has an area of about 1,15,000 sq km and has a population of over 3.5 crore.
